claims.text: The veterinary cordon fence (the Red Line) separates livestock-health zones and protects livestock to its south from foot-and-mouth disease and lung sickness. Movement, quarantine and processing requirements restrict access to some markets for northern livestock and meat, increasing costs and limiting buyers. These restrictions help explain differences in commercialisation, alongside land tenure, household objectives and infrastructure.

claims.text: Namibia’s Green Scheme develops irrigation along perennial rivers and at dams so that small-scale farmers can grow crops for sale alongside commercial operators; at Etunda near Ruacana in the Omusati Region, small-scale farmers each irrigate about 3 ha, growing crops such as maize, cabbage, tomatoes and onions; further projects lie along the Okavango River in the Kavango regions.

claims.text: Conservation agriculture, promoted on northern Namibian maize and mahangu fields, replaces ploughing with ripping narrow lines, keeps crop residues as soil cover and rotates cereals with legumes; ripping breaks the hard layer below the topsoil so water and roots go deeper, and trials in the Zambezi Region (2016/17-2019/20) found maize yields similar to ploughed fields.
